description: Red Moon believes stories stay alive when told. Every object humanity sent to space carried dreams, ideas and community, enduring thousands of kilometers away in crushing cold and solitude. Telling their stories keeps alive those who no longer can. We rescue abandoned hardware on the Moon, Mars and deep space, turning it into an educational experience where young explorers see these machines not as junk but as witnesses of our history and proof of human collaboration and aspiration.
summary: Our project is a campfire under the stars. Instead of cold data, we tell the stories of the machines we left behind on the Moon, Mars and deep space. Each one had a name, a purpose and a reason to travel so far from home. They were our eyes, our hands and sometimes our brave first steps into the unknown. We ask who they were, why they went and what they found. Their silence still speaks. Like footprints on a shore, their presence shows how far humanity has walked and how much we have learned together. By telling their stories in simple, human language, we turn abandoned hardware into companions and teachers. Their legacy helps us keep walking toward the universe, not as strangers, but as a community that remembers.
details:
Red Moon is a story-first experience that turns abandoned space hardware into something children can care about. It works like a quiet campfire under the stars. Each slide explains who it was, why it traveled so far, what it discovered and what it left behind. A playful “signal” interaction shows that most of these machines are silent now, while a few, like the Apollo laser retroreflectors, still answer us today.

The project benefits children, families and teachers by making space history accessible and emotional rather than technical. It connects STEM to empathy. It helps young readers see these objects not as junk but as witnesses of human curiosity, collaboration and courage. The intended impact is to keep their legacy alive and to inspire the next generation to keep exploring with humility and wonder.

We built the concept with React or Vue for the interface, Leaflet or Mapbox GL JS for the interactive map, and optional Three.js for a simple 3D view. Python with Pandas and GeoPandas helped us organize NASA location data. A light Node.js or Flask backend supports the content. Our main sources are NASA Trek, NSSDCA and NASA 3D Resources. We used our research document as a backstage script, not as the interface.

The creativity lies in the tone. Each object has a voice, a reason and a quiet afterlife. We used analogies like footprints on a shore and letters that never came back. We considered scientific accuracy, age-appropriate language, accessibility, low bandwidth, privacy and the need for a simple experience that works in classrooms without accounts. The final result is a set of simple, human and romantic slides that invite people to remember.
